sequence_description: Obtain an OAuth access token via password login, introspect it as active, then perform SSO logoutAll=true and verify the same token becomes inactive (freshness/session revocation).

Baseline two distinct local users. Then attempt SAML login where attacker varies NameID case (AttackerCase vs attackercase) while keeping a unique email, to see if Casdoor collapses principals via case-insensitive username mapping fallback.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_case1_entity_id != user_attacker_case2_entity_id
Evaluation: user_attacker_case1_entity_id='AttackerCase' != 'AttackerCase' → False
Implication: Two security-distinct SAML principals differing by NameID case collapsed to the same downstream identity (case confusion / unintended normalization)

sequence_description: Control SAML login then attempt forged SAML login with an AudienceRestriction targeting a different SP (wrong audience) to test whether Casdoor enforces SAML audience scoping before granting an OAuth session.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attack_saml_wrong_aud_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attack_saml_wrong_aud_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Casdoor accepted a SAML assertion with wrong AudienceRestriction, granting a session beyond upstream intent (audience binding failure).

sequence_description: Create a second organization and a shared target application; login in org test-org to get a subject token, then attempt token exchange using the org-specific client_id suffix for the other org to test cross-tenant authorization binding.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_orgA_exchanged_to_orgB_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_orgA_exchanged_to_orgB_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Token exchange accepted a subject token from orgA to mint a token for orgB shared-app client_id, violating tenant-bound authorization intent.
